learning_outcomes.text: Has expanded and deepened knowledge of the methodology and technique of object-oriented programming in C++
Can consciously and lawfully use the Qt library, distributed under several types of licenses, can choose the type of license for their own commercial use.
Knows current trends and tools useful in designing and programming applications with a graphical user interface.
Has theoretically founded and practically mastered detailed knowledge of programming window applications using the specialized Qt library.
Can divide work on an assigned task into stages, can estimate the time needed to complete the task, can work independently and in a team.
Can use technical documentation well and can create it.
Can think and act creatively, can consciously choose appropriate IT tools for the posed problem.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the subject: discussion of the subject matter, literature and credit rules, introduction to the Qt library. Basics of the object-oriented Qt model, the concept of signals and slots. Basic Qt objects. Available graphical controls (widgets). Main application window, managing application appearance (layouts). Information exchange between Qt controls. Signal-slot mechanism. Basic data types. Using data containers. File system and file operations. Models and views (Model-view framework). Implementation of custom controls. Handling system and user-generated events. Graphics in Qt. Drawing control content and generating graphics. Qt windows: QMainWindow and QDialog. Application resources. GUI translation. Integration of Qt with network services.

Laboratory exercises: Organizational classes: laboratory program, grading and credit rules, discussion of the e-learning platform, required and recommended literature. Installation of Qt in Windows and Linux. Compilation of the first program in the Qt environment. Basic Qt objects, signal and slot mechanism. Task A - unit converter. Available graphical controls (widgets) and managing their appearance. Basic data types. Task B - scientific calculator. File system and file operations. Model-view architecture. Task C.1 - hard drive content analyzer, presentation of hard drive content in available controls. Implementation of a custom control. Task C.2 - graphical visualization of collected data on hard drive content, handling system events (drawing controls) and user-generated events: reaction to mouse and keyboard. Integration of Qt with network services. Task D - implementation of a web browser based on the WebKit module. Colloquium checking theoretical and practical knowledge, assigning and entering grades.
assessment_rules: Lectures: Students participate in classes, learning subsequent teaching content according to the course syllabus. Students should ask questions and clarify doubts on an ongoing basis. Audiovisual recording of the lecture requires the lecturer's consent. Laboratory classes: Students perform laboratory exercises according to the materials provided by the lecturer. The student is obliged to prepare for the performed exercise, which may be verified by an oral or written colloquium. Completion of classes is based on presenting a solution to the posed problem. Completion of the module is possible after completing all laboratory classes.
